newsitem.title: MACAU: China, Portugal at odds over passports in Macau.
newsitem.headline: China, Portugal at odds over passports in Macau.

text.p: China and Portugal are at odds over the status of Macau residents holding Portuguese passports after the territory is handed back to Beijing in 1999.

The Sino-Portuguese Joint Liaison Group (JLG), a body handling matters related to Macau's handover, failed to agree in a meeting last week on the provisions given to Macau people with Portuguese nationality after the handover.
Portuguese-administered Macau will revert to China on December 20, 1999. Of some 110,000 Portuguese-passport holders in Macau, 90 percent are ethnic Chinese.
At the meeting, Portugal maintained that these Macau people can opt to retain their Portuguese nationality, which grants them consular protection.
But China, which does not recognise dual nationality, was adamant that ethnic Chinese in Macau can only use their Portuguese passports as travel documents, and not for consular protection.
